description: Patients who have at least one examination whose recorded ANA pattern is something other than S.

b.request: Patients who have at least one examination record where ANA Pattern is not equal to 'S'.
b.sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.* FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON p.ID = e.ID WHERE e.`ANA Pattern` != 'S'
b.raw: Patients who have at least one examination record where ANA Pattern is not equal to 'S'.

d.request: Patients with at least one examination where ANA Pattern is not equal to 'S', displaying their ID and sex, with the arithmetic mean of aCL IgM calculated across all their examinations (treating null values as absent), grouped by patient ID and sex, ordered by mean aCL IgM in descending order with null averages appearing last, showing the top 10 rows.
d.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) AS mean_acl_igm FROM Patient p INNER JOIN Examination e ON p.ID = e.ID WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT DISTINCT e2.ID FROM Examination e2 WHERE e2.`ANA Pattern` IS NOT NULL AND e2.`ANA Pattern` != 'S') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY mean_acl_igm IS NULL, mean_acl_igm DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: For patients with at least one examination record whose `ANA Pattern` is recorded and is something other than 'S', list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `aCL IgM` across all of their examinations (ignoring missing values, unrounded). Group by patient ID and sex, sort by that average from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10.
a.sql: SELECT e.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) as avg_acl_igm FROM Examination e INNER JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE e.ID IN (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Examination WHERE `ANA Pattern` IS NOT NULL AND `ANA Pattern` != 'S') GROUP BY e.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY CASE WHEN AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: Among patients whose examinations don't show an `ANA Pattern` of 'S', list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `aCL IgM` across all of their examinations (ignoring missing values, unrounded). Group by patient ID and sex, sort by that average from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10. Patients who have at least one examination whose recorded ANA pattern is something other than S.
c.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) as avg_aCL_IgM FROM Patient p INNER JOIN Examination e ON p.ID = e.ID WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT DISTINCT e2.ID FROM Examination e2 WHERE e2.`ANA Pattern` IS NOT NULL AND e2.`ANA Pattern` != 'S') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY avg_aCL_IgM DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10
